name: Back Bend Pose
intro:
Back Bend Pose (Ardha Chakrasana) is a gentle yet powerful yoga posture that focuses on opening the chest, stretching the spine, and improving overall flexibility. This pose involves bending the upper body backward while maintaining balance and control, making it an excellent posture for improving posture and spinal mobility.

It helps counteract the effects of prolonged sitting and slouching by expanding the chest and strengthening the back muscles. The backward stretch stimulates the nervous system, boosts energy levels, and enhances lung capacity by opening up the chest region.

Regular practice of back bends improves spinal flexibility, strengthens the core and lower back, and promotes better posture. It also helps in relieving mild back pain, reducing stress, and improving overall body awareness. When practiced mindfully, it creates a sense of openness and confidence both physically and mentally.

steps.text: Start by standing straight in Mountain Pose (Tadasana).
Place your hands on your lower back for support.
Inhale and gently lift your chest upward.
Slowly bend backward from the upper back.
Keep your neck relaxed and look upward.
Hold the pose while maintaining steady breathing.

benefits: Improves flexibility of the spine and back muscles
Opens the chest and improves lung capacity
Strengthens lower back and core muscles
Helps improve posture and body alignment
Reduces stiffness caused by long sitting hours
Stimulates nervous system and improves alertness
avoid: You have severe back pain or spinal injuries
You suffer from dizziness or vertigo
You have high blood pressure (consult a doctor)
You have neck injuries or discomfort
You are recovering from recent surgery
You feel pain while bending backward
You have hernia or serious abdominal issues
